hangar.compute.v1alpha1.ContainerPort.description: ContainerPort is a port the container listens on.

name.description: DNS-1123 label, unique within the container.

public.description: Expose the port over HTTPS through a PRIVATE PublicEndpoint the container owns, named "<container>-<name>". TCP only.

hangar.compute.v1alpha1.ContainerSpec.description: ContainerSpec is the desired state of a container.

image.description: OCI image reference. Changing it rebuilds the root disk. A tag is resolved when the container first runs it; to pick up a tag that moved since, name the image by its new digest or another tag.

imagePullSecrets.description: Names Secrets of type registry-auth, in the container's project, whose logins its node pulls the image with: the first that holds a login for the image's registry. Changing them restarts nothing; they count at the next pull. See docs/decisions/secrets.md.

interfaces.description: The networks the container is on, at most 8, each once; empty is one interface on "default". The first holds the default route. Changing them restarts the container, except when only their aliases change.

restartPolicy.description: RestartPolicy says when a container's process is restarted after it exits.

runState.description: Whether the container should be running; unset is RUNNING. Stopping sends the process SIGTERM, SIGKILL after a grace, and powers the VM off for good: the restart policy never brings a stopped container back. The root disk is kept, and RUNNING boots it again. Apply replaces the whole spec, so applying a manifest that leaves this out starts the container. The status condition Stopped says when a stop has taken effect.

volumes.description: The Disks and FileShares the container mounts, at most 8, as a Compose service's volumes in their long syntax. A disk is mounted by one machine at a time, and pins the container to the disk's node; a share must be on one of its networks and on a node, to which it pins the container; one on no node yet holds the container back. Changing them restarts the container. See docs/decisions/container-volumes.md.

hangar.compute.v1alpha1.ContainerStatus.description: ContainerStatus is the observed state of a container.

placement.description: The hardware of the node the container is placed on, as that node describes it now; unset until it is placed.

hangar.compute.v1alpha1.ContainerVolume.description: ContainerVolume is a volume a container mounts, as Compose writes one.

source.description: Names what is mounted, in the container's project: a Disk, unless source_kind says otherwise.

sourceKind.description: The kind source names. Hangar's, not Compose's: "Disk", which empty means, or "FileShare", which is mounted over NFS, nosuid and nodev, and never filled from the image.

target.description: Where the volume is mounted: an absolute path, neither / nor under /proc, /sys, /dev or /run, resolved as the image's processes resolve it, and made if it is missing.

type.description: "volume", the only type for now; empty means it. "bind" and "tmpfs" are refused.

hangar.compute.v1alpha1.ContainerVolumeO.description: ContainerVolumeOptions are a Compose volume's own options.

nocopy.description: Leaves a new volume empty, rather than filled with what the image has at the target. Always so for a file share.

subpath.description: Mounts this directory of the volume, a relative path, which must exist, instead of the whole volume.

hangar.compute.v1alpha1.NetworkInterface.description: NetworkInterface is one network interface a Container or VirtualMachine asks for. Its name is eth0, eth1… by position; its address comes from the network's range.

aliases.description: More names the network's resolver answers for the machine with its addresses on this network, A for its IPv4 address and AAAA for its public IPv6 one, as <alias>.<project>.hangar.internal, as it answers its name: at most 8, each a DNS label. Another machine with an interface on the network may hold none of them, as an alias or as its name; on another network the same alias names another machine. Other networks' resolvers do not know them. Changing them restarts nothing. See docs/decisions/networking.md.

network.description: Names a network in the object's project.

securityGroups.description: SecurityGroups of the network the interface is in; empty is the network's implicit "default" alone. Naming others without "default" leaves it.

hangar.compute.v1alpha1.Placement.description: Placement describes the hardware of a machine's host, never its load; every tenant with a machine on the node reads it. Fields are at most 64 printable characters. See docs/decisions/machine-placement.md.

chassis.description: Names the host's chassis, a DNS-1123 label such as "generic-1u-2x-u2"; a client draws one it does not know, or none, as a generic server.

cpuGeneration.description: The CPU's microarchitecture and code name, such as "Example Gen 3": known to the node agent for the CPUs it has a name for, or from the node's configuration.

cpuModel.description: The CPU as the host names it, without its core count, such as "Example CPU 1000".

memory.description: The kind of the host's memory, never its size, such as "DDR4-3200 ECC".

network.description: The host's Ethernet ports by the most speed each supports, never its link's, such as "2 × 10 GbE".

region.description: The region the host is in, such as "region-1", from the node's configuration.

site.description: The site within the region, such as a datacenter's name "site-a", from the node's configuration.

storage.description: The host's disks by kind, such as "2 × NVMe SSD".

hangar.compute.v1alpha1.Resources.description: Resources sizes the microVM. Each field is a quantity in Kubernetes syntax, such as "2", "512Mi" or "10Gi"; empty takes the default.

cpu.description: Whole vCPUs: "2" or "2000m", never a fraction.

disk.description: Root disk size, at least 1Gi. It can grow but never shrink.

hangar.meta.v1.Condition.description: Condition is one observed aspect of an object's state, such as "Ready".

observedGeneration.description: The generation this condition was computed from.

reason.description: CamelCase machine-readable cause of the last transition.

status.description: ConditionStatus is the state of a condition.

hangar.meta.v1.ObjectMeta.description: ObjectMeta is the metadata every resource carries. Users set name, project, labels and annotations; everything else is owned by the system. See docs/decisions/apply-semantics.md.

annotations.description: Keys under a *.hangarlab.cloud/ prefix are reserved for the system.

deleteTime.description: Set when deletion was requested and finalizers are still pending.

generation.description: Incremented on every change to spec.

labels.description: Keys under a *.hangarlab.cloud/ prefix are reserved for the system.

name.description: DNS-1123 label, unique within the project (or the platform, for global kinds). An Invitation's is an email instead.

resourceVersion.description: Store revision of the last write to this object.

hangar.meta.v1.OwnerReference.description: OwnerReference points at the object that owns this one. An owner is in the same project, a global object, or, for a global object, one in the project the reference names; when it is deleted, its dependents are garbage collected.

controller.description: The owner is the controller responsible for this object.

project.description: The owner's project, when the owner is project-scoped and this object is global, as a RoleBinding owned by the ServiceToken it names. Empty otherwise.

description: Container runs an OCI image as its own microVM. See docs/decisions/machine-model.md.
title: Container
